skill.author: callstackincubator

security_audit.summary: Three static findings permit command injection through directly interpolated action inputs; the other 75 matches are legitimate build operations or documentation. A separate semantic finding identifies unchecked multiline values that can overwrite workflow outputs and alter downstream settings. No evidence found of malicious intent, credential exfiltration, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Action inputs are interpolated directly into Bash source, including variant, scheme, and configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Pass inputs and outputs through step environment variables, then use quoted Bash expansions. Apply this throughout both composite actions and the caller workflow.

remediation.issue: Unchecked line breaks in identifiers, project settings, and build inputs can introduce additional workflow outputs or overwrite existing values.
remediation.suggestion: Reject carriage returns and line feeds before writing single-line outputs. Validate project paths, identifiers, schemes, configurations, and variants against expected values.

semantic_findings.title: Workflow Output Injection Through Unchecked Line Breaks
semantic_findings.description: Unvalidated identifiers and build inputs are written as single-line GITHUB_OUTPUT entries. Embedded newlines can introduce additional keys or overwrite existing outputs, changing downstream project paths, build selectors, or artifact metadata.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The templates append arbitrary strings with echo and do not reject line breaks. GitHub interprets additional key=value lines as separate outputs; exploitation requires control of those strings.

content.user_title: Build React Native CI Artifacts with GitHub Actions
content.value_statement: Mobile teams need repeatable simulator and emulator builds that testers can download. This skill provides reusable GitHub Actions templates and authenticated artifact retrieval examples.
actual_capabilities: Provide an iOS composite action template using Xcode simulator builds and app archive packaging.
Provide an Android composite action template using React Native project discovery and Gradle build variants.
Wire both platform jobs into push, pull request, and manual dispatch workflows.
Expose uploaded artifact names, IDs, and URLs through action outputs and workflow summaries.
Show authenticated artifact listing and downloads with gh CLI and the GitHub REST API.
Explain common Xcode scheme, Gradle variant, CocoaPods, and artifact packaging failures.
limitations: The skill supplies documentation and templates, not a hosted build service or verified build results.
iOS builds require macOS and Xcode; Android builds require Java, the Android SDK, and a Gradle wrapper.
Examples target React Native CLI simulator and emulator artifacts, not App Store or Play Store release delivery.
Templates require project-specific configuration, safe shell input handling, and workflow-output validation before accepting untrusted values.

use_cases.title: Create mobile pull request builds
use_cases.description: Adapt both composite action templates to produce downloadable iOS simulator apps and Android APKs for pull request validation.

use_cases.title: Standardize mobile CI pipelines
use_cases.description: Configure runners, dependency installation, build selectors, retention periods, and artifact metadata across both platform jobs.

use_cases.title: Retrieve test builds reliably
use_cases.description: Use run IDs, artifact names, or artifact IDs to retrieve the correct authenticated build archives for testing.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the build prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Use github-actions to identify prerequisites for this React Native repository. List required runners, dependencies, the iOS scheme, and the Android variant.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare a repository for mobile CI.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Android build action
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the Android composite action for this repository using the Debug variant. Expose artifact metadata and pass shell inputs through quoted environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Connect both platform workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a two-platform workflow using these references. Add pull request and manual triggers, seven-day artifact retention, read-only permissions, and safe shell input handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: build an integrated mobile CI pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Review artifact retrieval and security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this mobile workflow for input injection and artifact selection errors. Propose fixes and authenticated download steps using run IDs and artifact IDs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review an existing pipeline and retrieval process.

output_examples.input: Plan simulator and emulator builds for a React Native pull request.
output: iOS: use a macOS runner, install dependencies, select the shared Xcode scheme, and package the simulator app as a compressed archive.
Android: use a Linux runner with Java 17, install dependencies, and build the Debug APK through the project Gradle wrapper.
Artifacts: retain uploads for seven days and publish names, IDs, and authenticated URLs in the workflow summary.
Security: transfer dynamic inputs through environment variables instead of inserting them directly into Bash source.

output_examples.input: Explain how QA should retrieve a particular build artifact.
output: Identify the workflow run and inspect its artifact names, IDs, and expiration status.
Authenticate with GitHub and download by run ID plus artifact name, or use the REST endpoint with the artifact ID.
Confirm the selected artifact matches the intended platform and build configuration before testing.

output_examples.input: Diagnose an Android build that reports an unknown assembledebug task.
output: The Gradle variant uses incorrect casing.
Use Debug rather than debug so the generated task matches the project variant.
Check the module name reported by React Native configuration before retrying.

best_practices: Pass dynamic shell values through environment variables, quote expansions, validate build selectors, and reject line breaks in single-line workflow outputs.
Use read-only repository permissions and authenticate artifact downloads with appropriately scoped credentials.
Confirm project schemes and variants, package iOS apps as archives, and retain stable artifact names and IDs.
anti_patterns: Insert untrusted action inputs or job outputs directly into Bash source.
Treat authenticated artifact URLs as public download links or expose tokens in logs.
Assume default schemes, module names, variants, and runner toolchains match every repository.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill run a hosted build service?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and guidance that you adapt and run through your own GitHub Actions workflows.

faq.question: Does it produce store-ready mobile releases?
faq.answer: The documented templates target iOS simulator app archives and Android emulator APKs. Store signing and release delivery are not covered.

faq.question: What runner requirements apply?
faq.answer: iOS requires macOS with Xcode. Android requires a compatible Linux runner, Java 17, the Android SDK, and the project Gradle wrapper.

faq.question: How can I download a build artifact?
faq.answer: Authenticate with GitHub, then use gh CLI with the run ID and artifact name, or the REST API with the artifact ID.

faq.question: Can I use the templates unchanged?
faq.answer: Set repository-specific schemes, variants, and dependencies first. Replace direct shell interpolation with environment variables and reject line breaks in single-line outputs.
